title: Say it with a frame
prompt:
Draw a box around one word read from input. For the input `hello`:

```
+------------+
| hello      |
+------------+
```

The starter reads the word into `word_buf` and already holds the middle line's format string, `fmt_mid`. Add a border string to `.data` (a `+`, twelve `-`, a `+`), then print three lines: the border, the middle line, and the border again. One border string is enough; load its address into `x0` a second time for the bottom line.

`printf` prints exactly the characters it is given and never adds a line break of its own, so the border string needs its own `\n`. In `fmt_mid`, `%-10s` is replaced by the string whose address is in `x1`, padded with spaces to 10 characters, which keeps the right edge in place for any word. The starter's `scanf` cuts a longer word to its first 10 characters.

## what is checked

- with input `hello` the output is exactly the three lines above
- the program exits cleanly
- the program also runs on words you do not see: one of exactly 10 letters, one longer than 10, and no word at all
starter:
// draw a box around one word read from input
define(fp, x29)
define(lr, x30)

.data
fmt_in:     .string "%10s"
fmt_mid:    .string "| %-10s |\n"

.bss
word_buf:   .skip 11                        // up to 10 characters and the zero byte

.text
        .balign 4
        .global main
main:
        stp     fp, lr, [sp, -16]!
        mov     fp, sp

        ldr     x0, =fmt_in                 // read one word, cut to 10 characters
        ldr     x1, =word_buf
        bl      scanf

        // TODO: add a border string to .data, then print three lines:
        // the border, fmt_mid with the address of word_buf in x1,
        // and the border again

        mov     w0, 0
        ldp     fp, lr, [sp], 16
        ret
